etymologies.etymologyHTML: From main +‎ stream.

definitions.definition: Used or accepted broadly rather than by small portions of population, market, scientific community, etc.

quote.citation: 2011, Taner Edis, Science and Nonbelief, Greenwood Publishing Group, →ISBN, page 153:
quote.text: As unsubstantiated claims receive significant backing, skeptics and defenders of mainstream science enter the fray.

quote.citation: 2021 December 29, Stephen Roberts, “Stories and facts behind railway plaques: Aylesbury (2009)”, in RAIL, number 947, page 61:
quote.text: The mainstream media hones in on bad news stories where UK railways are concerned, yet gives scant attention to the many items of good news emerging from the network.

quote.citation: 2022 April 20, Rim-Sarah Alouane, “Marine Le Pen Is as Dangerous as Ever”, in The New York Times‎[1], →ISSN:
quote.text: If Ms. Le Pen looks more mainstream now, it’s because the mainstream looks more like her.

definitions.definition: The principal current in a flow, such as a river or flow of air
(usually with the) That which is common; the norm.

quote.citation: 1988 September 30, Tom Wicker, quoting George H. W. Bush, “Ol' Man Mainstream”, in The New York Times‎[2], →ISSN:
quote.text: George Herbert Walker Bush of Phillips Andover Academy and Yale University proclaimed in the first Presidential candidates' debate that he was “in touch with the mainstream of America.”

quote.citation: 1991 July 14, Andrew Pollack, “A Quirky Loner Goes Mainstream”, in The New York Times‎[3], →ISSN:
quote.text: Long content with being the BMW of the computer industry, suppying finely crafted machines to a relatively small number of fanatic customers, Apple now wants to become a Ford or Toyota, to move into the mainstream.

quote.citation: 2021 October 20, Dr Joseph Brennan, “A key part of our diverse railway heritage”, in RAIL, number 942, page 55:
quote.text: "Railways seldom slavishly followed styles to be seen in the mainstream of contemporary architecture," HE [Historic England] explains.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To popularize, to normalize, to render mainstream.

quote.citation: 2011, Jeff Change, Can't Stop Won't Stop: A History of the Hip-Hop Generation, page 420:
quote.text: Just as the gang peace movement desired to mainstream hardcore bangers into civic society, The Chronic wanted to drive hardcore rap into the popstream.

quote.citation: 2013, Catherine L. Albanese, America: Religions and Religion, 5th edition, Boston: Cengage Learning, →ISBN, page 262:
quote.text: In a nonchurch context, we can look more explicitly at formerly New Age practices to see if and how they have mainstreamed.

definitions.definition: (transitive, education, chiefly US) To educate (a disabled student) together with non-disabled students.

quote.citation: 1985 April 14, Barbara Gerbasi, “Mainstreaming My Son”, in The New York Times‎[4], →ISSN:
quote.text: Despite these beliefs, the decision to send my son to a regular school was not made easily. I didn't know of any child as disabled as he who had been mainstreamed.
